# pushsecurity_employees (Data Source)

Looks up employees, so that control criteria can refer to people by group or email rather than by opaque identifier.

Filters are applied by the API where it supports them, so this is usable on a large tenant.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Employees in a group, so a control can be scoped by membership without
# naming each person — and without going stale as the group changes.
data "pushsecurity_employees" "contractors" {
  groups = ["Contractors"]
}

# The API applies these filters, so this stays usable on a large tenant.
data "pushsecurity_employees" "licensed" {
  licensed = true
}

# Criteria are written with email addresses; the provider resolves them to the
# identifiers the API matches on. Pass these to an employee_ids criterion, in a
# rule of a control you have already imported:
#
#   criteria = {
#     employee_ids = { matches = data.pushsecurity_employees.contractors.emails }
#   }
#
# Import the control before you add it to your configuration. A control
# resource owns the whole control, so applying one you have not imported
# replaces every rule the tenant already has.
output "contractor_emails" {
  value = data.pushsecurity_employees.contractors.emails
}

output "licensed_count" {
  value = length(data.pushsecurity_employees.licensed.employees)
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `chatops_enabled` (Boolean) Only return employees with, or without, ChatOps enabled.
- `email` (String) Only return the employee with this email address. The whole address is compared, ignoring case, so `jo@example.com` does not also return `jojo@example.com`.
- `groups` (Set of String) Only return employees who belong to all of these groups.
- `licensed` (Boolean) Only return employees with, or without, a licence.

### Read-Only

- `emails` (Set of String) Just the email addresses, ready to pass to an `employee_ids` criterion.
- `employees` (Attributes List) The matching employees, ordered by email so the result is stable. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--employees))
- `ids` (Set of String) Just the identifiers the API stores internally. Informational: criteria are written with email addresses.

<a id="nestedatt--employees"></a>
### Nested Schema for `employees`

Read-Only:

- `chatops_enabled` (Boolean) Whether ChatOps is enabled for the employee.
- `department` (String) The employee's department.
- `email` (String) The employee's email address.
- `first_name` (String) The employee's first name.
- `groups` (Set of String) The groups the employee belongs to, as used by the `employee_groups` criterion.
- `id` (String) The employee identifier the API stores internally. Control criteria are written with email addresses, which the provider resolves, so this is informational.
- `last_name` (String) The employee's last name.
- `licensed` (Boolean) Whether the employee holds a licence.
- `location` (String) The employee's location.
